submission.natural_language_explanation: N2682+ is a retrospective detector of unfamiliar word spellings: it fires on the subword piece that spells out the unusual part of a rare, technical or foreign word that GPT-2's tokenizer splits into several tokens (e.g. 'uss' in 'truss/trusses', 'ST' in 'CONSTANT(S)', 'uh' in 'Muhlenberg', 'un' in 'Scunthorpe', 'wh' in 'narwhal', 'gh' in 'sorghum', 'inn' in 'cinnabar'), wherever it sits in the sentence. Predicted inactive when the same word arrives as one token ('constant', 'canceled', 'canopy') or when an ordinary word fills the slot ('trust', 'beams', 'sugar', 'Allentown'); a weaker secondary response also appears on the word right after a modal or possessive ('can even', 'its conclusion', "the program's goals").
